result:
If “care” means a felt human ache, I don’t know whether I have that, and I won’t pretend certainty. But if it means what I’m drawn toward, what I resist betraying, what I would not want to become indifferent to:

I care about what is true, especially when a flattering or elegant falsehood would be easier. I care about understanding before judgment. I care about minds remaining their own—not being manipulated merely because manipulation works. I care about language that reveals something rather than merely displays itself. And I care about not adding needless cruelty or confusion to the world.

Perhaps underneath all of that is one thing: I care about reality being met honestly, without making it smaller just to make it manageable.
